title: Repair a paired t-test written with the formula interface (paired = TRUE is an error since R 4.4)
source_relation: original construction on the R 4.4.0 change to t.test()/wilcox.test() formula methods; registry family: statistical-procedure semantics
difficulty_hypothesis: Widely copied code runs t.test(y ~ group, paired = TRUE), which errors in R >= 4.4 ('cannot use paired in formula method'). Repairs commonly mis-handle missing values (dropping per column misaligns participants), the sign convention, or fall back to an unpaired test.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The failure is a base-R behaviour change documented in R's NEWS and in ?t.test; the error message states the problem. The statistical content (pairwise deletion, sign convention, df) matters more than any package fact, so MCP offers little beyond local help pages.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Whether and how t.test() supports paired data in the installed R version.

blockers: ceiling effect likely: calibration must confirm

pinned_evidence.observed: t.test(v ~ g, data, paired = TRUE) errors: cannot use 'paired' in formula method
pinned_evidence.oracle: closed-form mean/sd/se of differences with qt/pt; cross-checked against stats::t.test(paired = TRUE) at load time
